key_insight: Create compact, semantically meaningful 3D 'proxy' representations by clustering multi-view visual features and aligning those proxies with language embeddings, enabling spatially consistent 3D reasoning for vision-language models without heavy per-pixel 3D processing.
problem_solved: Addresses poor spatial consistency and high computational cost of existing VLM 3D approaches—correspondence-based methods lack stable 3D semantics, while geometry-heavy representation methods are inefficient for long image/sequence inputs.
method: Aggregate multi-view/pixel features into a small set of semantic 3D proxies via clustering in combined geometric+feature space (centroids encode position + semantic embedding).
Align the proxy embeddings with language representations (contrastive or cross-attention) so VLMs can ground text to compact 3D entities instead of dense pixels or explicit meshes.
Use the proxy set as an efficient intermediate representation for downstream tasks, enabling faster inference and scalable sequence processing while preserving spatial consistency.
impact: Makes 3D-aware vision-language models more practical by reducing compute and memory while improving spatial grounding—beneficial for 3D QA, visual grounding, robotics and any application needing scalable spatial reasoning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view images → feature extraction → semantic clustering → 3D proxy nodes → alignment with text
Before/after comparison: dense pixel/mesh approach vs compact proxy representation (bars for compute, memory, latency)
Qualitative examples: text queries and spatial grounding overlays showing improved consistency across views
Schematic icon set: proxy nodes (dots), language token alignment (lines), speed/efficiency badge
paper_title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment
paper_authors: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno
